findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0-anonymous restriction on website
findings.description:
`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109). For a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous guardian, the generated `include_website?` returns false through `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (`lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60`). The new `website_name` is declared at line 43 but is not added to that list. Its include method (lines 153-155) checks only `website.present?`, so for the same user it still serializes the host and path. `UsersController#show` builds `UserSerializer` with the requesting guardian (`app/controllers/users_controller.rb:33`), so `/users/:username.json` returns the value to anonymous visitors. The "TL0 seen as anonymous" spec (`spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:6-16`) iterates a hard-coded list that omits `website_name`, so it does not catch this.

Fix: add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, delete the hand-written `include_website_name` (the generated `include_website_name?` then checks both restriction and presence), and add `website_name` to the spec list at line 11.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing its `?` and is never called
findings.description:
Every other include predicate in `app/serializers` uses the `include_<attr>?` form, for example `include_email?` at line 117 and `include_card_image_badge_id?` at line 161. AMS 0.8.3 (`Gemfile.lock:22`) defines a default `include_<attr>?` that returns true when `attributes` declares the attribute, which happens at line 43. The bare `include_website_name` is therefore dead code, and the `website.present?` gate never runs. `website_name` is always in the JSON, as `null` for users with no website. The template hides this with `{{#if model.website_name}}`.

I could not confirm this against the gem source. A spec asserting that `json` has no `:website_name` key for a user without a website would settle it.

findings.title: Profile header label does not update after the website is edited
findings.description:
The removed `websiteName` property depended on `model.website`, so it updated as the value changed. `model.website_name` is set only by `findDetails` (`routes/user.js.es6:54`). The preferences form binds `model.website` directly (`templates/user/preferences.hbs:158`). `preferences` is nested under `user` (`routes/app-route-map.js.es6:56,74`), so this header stays on screen while the form is edited. The save path (`models/user.js.es6:166-217`) does not refresh `website_name`, and the parent `user` route's `afterModel` does not re-run on child-route transitions.

The result is that the `href` updates while the visible label keeps the old value until a full reload. Setting `self.set('website_name', data.user.website_name)` in the save's `then` would fix it. The PUT renders `UserSerializer` (`users_controller.rb:100`), so the value should be in the response.

findings.title: Spec coverage misses the untrusted case and most of the branch logic
findings.description:
- `website_name` is absent from the untrusted list at line 11, so the privacy regression above is not guarded.
- No test covers a blank or nil website, which is where the missing-`?` gate bug shows.
- The middle branch (`user_serializer.rb:144-146`, "www.example.com == forum.example.com") has no test, even though the comment describes it.
- A website that is a subdomain of the forum's domain, such as `www.example.com` on `example.com`, falls through to host-only output (line 149). The reverse, `example.com` on `forums.example.com`, gets the path. That asymmetry is not pinned by any test.

findings.title: website_name is hard to follow and duplicates URI parsing and path concatenation
findings.description:
`URI(website.to_s)` is parsed three times. `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` is repeated in three branches, and line 146 combines two ternaries on one line. The `rescue nil` modifier on line 138 swallows every error and assigns nil. Line 149 appends to a string literal in place with `"." << website_host`, which is safe only because literals are not frozen here.

Suggested cleanup: parse once into `uri`, rescue `URI::InvalidURIError` explicitly, move the parent-domain comparison into a small helper, and write the check as `discourse_host.end_with?(".#{website_host}")`.

findings.title: Host comparison is case-sensitive
findings.description: Ruby's `URI#host` keeps the case the user typed, and `format_url` (`app/services/user_updater.rb:105-106`) does not normalize it. A website of `http://Example.com/user` on forum `example.com` fails the equality check and falls to the else branch, which returns `Example.com` without the path. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so both sides should be downcased. This follows from reading the code and Ruby's `URI` behavior; I did not execute it.

findings.title: Displayed value changed from host-only to host plus path for same-site websites
findings.description: The removed client code (`website.split("/")[2]`) always showed the host only. The new logic returns `host/path` when the website is on the forum's domain or a parent of it. The specs encode this, so it looks intentional, but it is a visible change and should be called out in the PR description.

findings.title: websiteName removal is complete and the template is updated
findings.description: A search of the whole checkout found no remaining `websiteName` references in app, spec, or test code. The client-side URL parsing was removed, and the template uses the server value for both the link and the span. The `@property` doc comment at `models/user.js.es6:59` was also corrected from `websiteName` to `profileBackground`, which is accurate. This finding covers only the removal. The stale-label problem is reported separately above.
